proof:
The energy-root concavity and strict own concavity are 5aeb5916857f97a9. The finite canonical-roof Hausdorff continuity 7227bbfcd12ad3d2 and marked energy continuity b3c0088cf09b2894 give continuity through every own boundary, where the energy is zero. The joint concavity extends by continuity from the convex own-interior domain: the own interior is dense in each positive fiber. The function $G(l,F)=l^{1/N}F^{d/N}$ is concave on the nonnegative quadrant and is strictly increasing in $F$ when $l>0$. Applying this mean to the concave inputs and multiplying by $M^{-1/N}$ proves the assertions about $f$.

At $Y$ restrict to its own fiber. The one-sided directional derivative of $L$ in any continuous direction is the minimum of the scalar products of that direction with the active slopes, since inactive planes have a strict gap at $Y$. The directional derivative of $f$ is therefore the minimum of the scalar products with $f(Y)a_E+f(Y)c_r/(NL(Y))$, with $c_r$ running through the active continuous slopes. Here the ordinary energy derivative is $\nabla_x F=(N/d)F a_E$ by d7ff9f9aad2b6512. A supergradient $g$ majorizes every directional derivative, and separation from the convex hull of these slopes would give a direction violating that inequality. Thus $g$ is a convex combination of those slopes. The same coefficients on the full active $L$-planes give a global $L$ upper tangent with base part $\alpha_L$. The full upper tangent for $F$ from d7ff9f9aad2b6512 extends to all of $C$ by continuity. The supporting-plane inequality for the scalar concave mean $G$ at the positive pair $(L(Y),F(Y))$ now gives the displayed full upper tangent for $f$. Its coefficients in each input are positive.

At fixed old covariance whiten $X$ by $\Sigma^{-1/2}$ and carry the scalar profile along by composition. Covariance-unit normals become Euclidean unit, all masses gain the same determinant factor, and the assumed distance ensures the whitened own radius is greater than $\varepsilon f(Y)$. Apply the convex right-quantile region 0b2fbdaf8d3134a0 and finite active-cap balance c5ce541ffa55a29c, transporting the caps, thresholds and slopes back. In particular $I$ is lattice-complete by projecting convex combinations of deepest marks, and at each deepest mark $Y=(p,y)$ there is a positive cap balance $\sum_j\rho_j u_j=\varepsilon g$ and $c_j=N_j\cdot Y-\varepsilon f(Y)$. Take the full upper tangent $(\alpha,g)$ above. For any $(z,x)\in C$ the weighted margin is at least $(\sum_j\rho_j a_j-\varepsilon\alpha)\cdot(z-p)$. At every sampled deepest mark the weighted margin is nonpositive by the individual right-quantile inequalities. Thus the corrected base functional is nonpositive on $\operatorname{conv}I-p$ and vanishes on $F_p-p$, where $F_p$ is the minimal face containing $p$. The margin is consequently nonnegative on all fibers above $F_p$. At every deepest mark there it is zero, with each positively weighted quantile active. A sampled assigned fiber contains such an interior zero. Two interior zeros contradict strict own concavity of $f$. An additional boundary zero would force the convex nonnegative margin to vanish on the segment joining it to the interior zero, hence at two interior points, the same contradiction.

Select one deepest representative in the relative interior of each maximal occupied minimal face. If representatives of two different maximal faces have equal inherited parity, their midpoint is an integer point of $\operatorname{conv}I$ and hence in $I$. Its minimal face contains both endpoints and therefore both faces, violating maximality. Each point of $I$ belongs to some maximal occupied face. This gives the full cover and the parity count.

For continuation the current weights and profile converge uniformly on matched sampled marks by marked energy continuity and covariance and mass convergence, and every old interior contact remains in the current fiber. Compactness and testing those contacts imply $\alpha_i(t)\to0$ and every convergent sequence of its minimizers tends to an old zero. For the indicated signed paths the uniform expansion and finite-contact minimum of 5fa497a06b11cbcb apply on compact own-interior neighborhoods. Multiplying the profile term by $e^{st}$ adds $-s\varepsilon f(Y_{ia})$ at contact $a$ because $\sum_j\rho_{ij}\Gamma(u_{ij})=1$; uniformity is unchanged. The old proper cut of each cap crosses an interior ball in the group's representative fiber. A smaller ball and a common neighborhood of strictly decreasing tails persist under nearby normals and bodies. The moving tails converge uniformly in nearby thresholds, by symmetric-difference convergence plus the slab bound for the bounded plane displacements on the common bounded set. Each tail is continuous, and any threshold interval in this neighborhood removes a positive-volume slab of the retained ball. Its inverse near $Q$ is therefore the right quantile and is strictly decreasing and continuous, with convergence at each nearby fixed mass by bracketing thresholds. Bracketing the weighted sum on either side of $Q$ and using $\alpha_i(t)\to0$ proves existence, uniqueness and convergence of the solution. For each assigned current mark, the weighted margin above the corresponding moving quantiles is nonnegative by the minimum formula; at least one individual threshold is at least its quantile. That actual through-mark cap has mass at most $q_i(t)$. Uniform depth convergence on matched marks by f2ead43a963c7026 keeps a strict gap at the finite nondeepest bases. All $q_i(t)\to Q$, so the complete old covering set controls the current maximum.

statement:
Let $P$ be a nonempty finite complete affine-lattice base with positive compatible convex $d$-fibers $K_z$, $d\ge1$, canonical hull $C$ and summed mixed volume $dm$ of mass $M$. Compatibility means $\sum_z\lambda_zK_z\subset K_p$ whenever $\sum_z\lambda_zz=p\in P$ is a convex combination. Write $C_z$ for the fiber of $C$ at any real base $z$ and $\Gamma(u)=\sqrt{u^{\mathsf T}\Sigma u}$ for the pooled within-fiber covariance norm. Let $L>0$ be a finite minimum of affine functions on a neighborhood of $C$, with $\int\log L\,dm=0$. Put $N=d+1$ and $f(z,x)=(L(z,x) E_{C_z}(x)/M)^{1/N}$, using zero own-boundary projective energy. The profile is continuous and jointly concave on $C$, strictly concave on own interiors and positive precisely there. For an own-interior sampled mark $Y=(p,y)$, let $F=E_{C_z}(x)^{1/d}$ and $a_E$ be the minimizing projective parameter at $Y$. Every own supergradient of $f$ at $Y$ is $g=f(Y)a_E+f(Y)c/(NL(Y))$ for an own slope $c$ of a convex combination of the active affine $L$-planes. If $\alpha_L$ is the base slope of that combination and $(\alpha_F,\nabla_x F(Y))$ a full supergradient of $F$, then $(\alpha,g)$ is a full supergradient of $f$, with $\alpha=f(Y)\alpha_L/(NL(Y))+d f(Y)\alpha_F/(NF(Y))$.

Fix $\varepsilon>0$ and define buffered cap depth using threshold $a\cdot p+u\cdot y-\varepsilon\Gamma(u)f(p,y)$ for nonzero $u$ and unchanged closed pure-base caps. Let $Q$ be the maximum raw depth on sampled fibers and $I$ its deepest bases. Assume every deepest mark has own-interior distance $>\varepsilon f(Y)\sqrt{\lambda_{\max}(\Sigma)}$. Then $I$ is lattice-complete and admits a covering by at most $k(I)\le k(P)$ groups, with $k$ counting inherited parities. For each group $i$ there is an inclusion-maximal face $F_i$ of $\operatorname{conv}I$ among those with a sampled point in their relative interior. Assign it the finite set $J_i=I\cap F_i$, allowing overlaps. There are at most $d+1$ actual mass-$Q$ caps $N_{ij}\cdot w\ge c_{ij}$ in each group, with $\Gamma(u_{ij})=1$, right $Q$-quantile thresholds and positive weights $\rho_{ij}$ summing to one. Put $h_i=\sum_j\rho_{ij}c_{ij}$. The margin $\sum_j\rho_{ij}N_{ij}\cdot w-h_i-\varepsilon f(w)$ is nonnegative throughout every whole real fiber over $F_i$. On each sampled assigned fiber it has exactly one zero, at the own-interior deepest mark, where all selected quantiles are active.

Now move the compatible positive fibers on the same bases by $K_z(t)\to K_z$ in Hausdorff distance. Let $L_t$ be positive on the new hull, continuous there, and converge to $L$ on matched sampled marks uniformly. Let $N_{ij}(t)\to N_{ij}$ and $\varepsilon(t)\to\varepsilon$ be the current normals and scale, use the actual updated mass and covariance, and put $f_t=(L_t E_t/M_t)^{1/N}$ and $A_i(t)=\sum_j\rho_{ij}\Gamma_t(u_{ij}(t))$. Define
$$
\alpha_i(t)=\min_{z\in J_i,\ x\in K_z(t)}\left[\sum_j\rho_{ij}N_{ij}(t)\cdot(z,x)-h_i-\varepsilon(t)A_i(t)f_t(z,x)\right].
$$
All minimizers approach the finite old zeros. If the current objective is the one along the signed paths in 5fa497a06b11cbcb with $\varepsilon(t)=\varepsilon e^{st}$, its first coefficient is the minimum of their $A_{ia}-s\varepsilon f(Y_{ia})$. For all small $t$ there is a unique nearby mass $q_i(t)\to Q$ with $\sum_j\rho_{ij}c_{ij}(t,q_i(t))=h_i+\alpha_i(t)$, where $c_{ij}(t,q)$ are the actual right quantiles. The current depth on each assigned whole fiber is at most $q_i(t)$, the strict gaps at old nondeepest bases persist, and the current raw maximum is at most $\max_i q_i(t)$.
title: Full-parameter contact cover and its exact whole-fiber continuation
